title: TLT FinStress regime-dependent tracking via rolling 52-week DM

regime_definition.rationale: exogenous date-based split (E064) — avoids IS-cutoff degeneracy

verdict.label: H1
verdict.interpretation: TLT FinStress is regime-dependent — significant ONLY in rate-hike era
details: Post-2022 M4 vs M3 t=+5.675 Harvey-sig, Pre-2022 t=+0.722 NS
Block bootstrap (8wk, 1000 reps) Post-2022: 99.8% > Harvey +3; Pre-2022 only 2.6% — robust
verdict.self_check_DM_t_above_6_note: Preamble rule #5: DM-t > 6 triggers self-check. Post-2022 M4 vs M1 t=+8.054. Verified via: (a) block bootstrap 99.8% of samples confirm t>3, (b) rolling 52-week max only +2.98 (never single-window Harvey-sig), (c) Pre-2022 NS with 94.4% vs 35.4% of windows showing M4>M3. The +8.054 reflects regime-specific 104-week joint OOS fit; rolling 52-week max +2.98 is consistent with signal present but not dominating any single 52-week slice. Use post_2022_M4_vs_M3 t=+5.675 (bootstrap 99.8%>3) as primary evidence; treat the +8.054 vs M1 as reinforcing, not sole basis.

paper4_narrative_impact: Paper 4 must add regime caveat: TLT M4 IV-sufficiency is regime-contingent, holding during ZIRP but breaking during rapid tightening. Universal claim becomes 'IV sufficient except during rate-cycle inflection.'
